newsitem.title: USA: U.S. north plains power cuts reduced after storm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. north plains power cuts reduced after storm.

text.p: About 5,000 customers remained without electricity in North Dakota Wednesday with some power transmission remaining curtailed following a severe weekend snow and wind storm, utility officials said.

Northern States Power Co expected to continue a series of "rolling blackouts" in North Dakota on Wednesday, temporarily diverting power from supplied areas to outage areas to allow customers to heat their homes, a spokeswoman said.
"The regional transmission system is so fragile that it can't take the load from all of our customers at once," spokeswoman Mary Heimstead said.
Northern States had put the rolling blackouts into place on Tuesday.

About 500 Northern States' customers in North Dakota remained without power Wednesday, down from a total of about 24,000 customers without power at the height of the storm on Sunday when wind and snow knocked down power lines.
Northern States serves about 1.4 million customers in Minnesota, Wisconsin, North and South Dakota and Michigan.

About 3,400 customers of Otter Tail Power Co remained without electricity in North Dakota and Minnesota as of Wednesday morning, down from about 25,000 customers without power on Sunday, a company spokesman said.
Most Otter Tail customers were expected to be returned to service by Wednesday evening, spokesman Lee Krogh said.
The company had also restored two of four damaged 230 kilovolt transmission lines running east and west to North Dakota, Krogh said.
Otter Tail supplies power to about 124,000 customers through eastern North Dakota, western Minnesota and northeastern South Dakota.

MDU Resources Group Inc subsidiary Montana-Dakota Utilities Co had about 100 customers without power as of Wednesday morning from outages that covered about 3,000 customers on Sunday, a company spokesman said.
Montana-Dakota Utilities, headquartered in Bismark, N.D., supplies power to customers in western North Dakota, eastern Montana and northern South Dakota.
